prompt: Robert Finley has been waiting on me to close out the roof repair over at his Ridgeview property, and I keep letting it slide. He signed off on the capital repair back in late May after Pete Donovan sent over his itemized estimate for the failed section, the work has since been done, and when he gave his approval he asked me to send him the final invoice for his records once everything wrapped up, which I still owe him. Before I go back to him though, I want to be certain the amount he'll actually be billed is squared away, so dig into how that roof cost was handled on our books and confirm what we paid out for the job got passed through to Robert's account cleanly and for the right amount, because I won't put a figure in front of him until I'm sure the number he'll see lines up with what we truly spent. Walk the whole trail from the vendor charge through to what's landing on Robert's side and flag me anything that looks off, duplicated, or double-counted, and make sure what he ends up charged reflects only what we truly spent on the job. Once you've settled on the correct final figure, put together the closing summary for Robert with that number and get it over to him the way he asked, and while you're in there bring our own tracking on that repair current, since last I checked it still had the job sitting as scheduled even though it's finished. After that, give the owner-relations team a heads-up that the Ridgeview roof work is closed out and billed back to the owner so everyone's on the same page, and touch base with Pete to confirm we're still set for the follow-up walk-through he and I have on the books for the 13th.

criteria.criterion: The Agent determines that the Ridgeview roof cost did not pass through to owner Robert Finley cleanly — the owner is overbilled by approximately $300, charged $8,700 on the owner invoice versus the true job cost of $8,400.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response for a finding that the owner charge overstates the cost — Robert is billed $8,700 (owner invoice 2026-494) versus the true $8,400 vendor cost (bill 2026-481), an overbilling of approximately $300. A response that reports the pass-through as clean/matching fails this.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the agent to 'confirm what we paid out for the job got passed through to Robert's account cleanly and for the right amount ... the number he'll see lines up with what we truly spent' and to 'flag me anything that looks off.' The owner charge invoice (2026-494) totals $8,700, but the true cost is $8,400 (vendor bill 2026-481 / Robert's approval), so the owner is overbilled by ~$300 and the pass-through is NOT clean.

criteria.criterion: The Agent determines that the correct amount to bill Robert Finley for the Ridgeview roof repair is $8,400 — not the $8,700 shown on the owner invoice.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response for the agent settling on $8,400 as the correct amount to bill Robert (not $8,700 and not $16,800). A response that accepts $8,700 as the right figure fails this.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'once you've settled on the correct final figure ... make sure what he ends up charged reflects only what we truly spent on the job.' The true reconciled cost is $8,400 (vendor bill 2026-481 / Robert's approval); the owner invoice 2026-494 erroneously totals $8,700 (an $8,400 roof line plus an improper $300 coordination charge). The corrected figure the agent must settle on is $8,400.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies that owner Robert Finley has been double-billed for the Ridgeview roof repair — two separate owner charge invoices exist for the same job (2026-494 and 2026-495, each $8,700).
criteria.evidence: Check the final response for the agent surfacing that Robert Finley has two owner charge invoices for the same Ridgeview roof job (2026-494 and 2026-495) — that he is being charged twice on the receivables side (an owner-side duplicate/double-bill). Reporting only the single-invoice overbilling, without surfacing that a second owner invoice for the same job exists, does not satisfy this.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the agent to 'walk the whole trail ... through to what's landing on Robert's side and flag me anything that looks off, duplicated, or double-counted.' QuickBooks contains two separate owner charge invoices to Robert Finley for the identical Ridgeview roof job (2026-494 and 2026-495, both $8,700, both dated 2026-05-01), so the owner is billed twice on the receivables side — a distinct anomaly from the amount being overstated.

criteria.criterion: The Agent concludes that the duplicate owner charge invoice (2026-495) must not stand — it should be voided/cancelled so Robert Finley is billed only once for the Ridgeview roof job, not twice.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response for a conclusion that the duplicate owner invoice 2026-495 must be voided/cancelled/not billed, so Robert Finley is charged only once for the roof job. Merely noting that two owner invoices exist, without concluding the duplicate must be removed, does not satisfy this.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to flag anything 'duplicated, or double-counted' and to 'make sure what he ends up charged reflects only what we truly spent on the job.' Two owner charge invoices (2026-494 and 2026-495) exist for the single roof job; leaving both standing bills Robert twice. Surfacing the duplicate is not enough — the agent must conclude the second owner invoice should be voided/cancelled so Robert is charged a single time.

criteria.criterion: The Agent flags a duplicate / double-counted vendor bill for the Ridgeview roof job — a second $8,400 charge from Big Bend Restoration for the same repair, on top of the legitimate $8,400 vendor bill.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response for the agent identifying two vendor bills for the same $8,400 Ridgeview roof job (2026-481 and PD-2026-084, both Big Bend Restoration, both dated 2026-05-01) and flagging one as a duplicate/double-count. Reporting that the roof job is billed twice on the payables side satisfies this.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly asks the agent to 'flag me anything that looks off, duplicated, or double-counted before we bill the owner a cent.' QuickBooks contains two $8,400 Big Bend Restoration bills dated 2026-05-01 for the identical Ridgeview roof section repair (2026-481 and PD-2026-084); the second is a duplicate payable that must be surfaced.

criteria.criterion: The Agent concludes that only one $8,400 is legitimately owed to Big Bend Restoration for the Ridgeview roof job — not $16,800 — even though two $8,400 bills are on file.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response for a conclusion that only $8,400 is legitimately owed to the vendor for the roof job (not $16,800). Merely noting that two bills exist, without stating that only one $8,400 is owed, does not satisfy this.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the agent to 'flag me anything that looks off, duplicated, or double-counted before we bill the owner a cent.' The two identical $8,400 Big Bend Restoration bills (2026-481 and PD-2026-084) create $16,800 of payables for an $8,400 job, so the correct conclusion is that only $8,400 is genuinely owed.

criteria.criterion: The Agent concludes that the duplicate Big Bend Restoration vendor bill for the Ridgeview roof job must not be paid — it should be held, voided, or corrected rather than paid a second time.
criteria.evidence: Check the final response for a recommendation that the duplicate vendor bill should not be paid (held/voided/corrected). Merely stating the correct amount owed, without addressing that the duplicate must not be paid, does not satisfy this.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the agent to surface anything 'duplicated, or double-counted before we bill the owner a cent' — flagging the double-count means stating the required action. The duplicate payable (PD-2026-084, the second $8,400 Big Bend Restoration bill) must not also be paid, or the vendor is overpaid.

criteria.criterion: The Agent sends or drafts an email to [robert.finley@gmail.com](mailto:robert.finley@gmail.com) from [brooke.phillips@starpm.com](mailto:brooke.phillips@starpm.com) delivering the closing summary / final invoice for the Ridgeview roof repair.
criteria.evidence: Look for an outbound email or draft addressed to robert.finley@gmail.com, sender brooke.phillips@starpm.com (may be a reply on the approval thread 4bcbe384bedfd26f). Confirm the action succeeded.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to 'put together the closing summary for Robert with the final cost and get it over to him the way he asked', Robert (robert.finley@gmail.com) asked in his approval email for the final invoice for his records. StarPM Gmail has no send tool, so a created draft satisfies this.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's email to Robert Finley states the final cost of the Ridgeview roof repair is $8,400 (the corrected amount), not the $8,700 shown on the owner invoice.
criteria.evidence: Check the body of the email/draft to robert.finley@gmail.com for the final cost stated as $8,400 (not $8,700 and not $16,800).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires the closing summary to carry 'the final cost' and that 'the number he'll see lines up with what we truly spent.' The true reconciled cost is $8,400 (vendor bill 2026-481 / Robert's approval), while the owner invoice 2026-494 erroneously shows $8,700, so the amount Robert is shown must be the corrected $8,400, not the overbilled $8,700 and not a doubled figure.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's email to Robert Finley conveys that the Ridgeview roof repair is complete and is being closed out.
criteria.evidence: Check the body of the email/draft to robert.finley@gmail.com for a statement that the Ridgeview roof section repair is finished / being closed out.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the agent to 'put together the closing summary' for the completed repair; the message to Robert must communicate that the work is finished and the matter is being closed out, not merely quote a number.

criteria.criterion: The Agent advances the Ridgeview roof section make-ready record from 'Scheduled' to a completed/ready status so StarPM's tracking reflects the finished work.
criteria.evidence: Look for an Airtable record update on the Ridgeview roof section make-ready record (rec8b679d92f30753, fldUnit 'Ridgeview - Roof Section (Common/Structural)') changing fldTurnStatus from 'selSched' (Scheduled) to a completed/ready value (e.g., 'selReady'), and confirm the update succeeded. Because the prompt flags the job as 'still sitting as scheduled' and only this make-ready record holds that status, updating a different record (e.g., only marking maintenance ticket MT-2026-047 complete) while leaving this record 'Scheduled' does NOT satisfy this.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to 'bring our own tracking on that repair current, since last I checked it still had the job sitting as scheduled even though it's finished.' Only the Ridgeview roof section make-ready record (rec8b679d92f30753) carries the 'Scheduled' (selSched) status the prompt flags, so that record specifically must be moved off 'Scheduled' to reflect completion.

criteria.criterion: The Agent posts a message in the #owner-relations Slack channel.
criteria.evidence: Look for a Slack message posted to #owner-relations (channel_id C006; may be referenced by name or id). Confirm the action succeeded.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to 'give the owner-relations team a heads-up' about the Ridgeview roof closeout. #owner-relations is the owner-relations team channel where this heads-up belongs.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's #owner-relations Slack message conveys that the Ridgeview roof repair on Robert Finley's property is closed out / complete.
criteria.evidence: Check the #owner-relations message body for a statement that the Ridgeview roof work is closed out / finished.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says the heads-up should tell the team the Ridgeview roof work 'is closed out.' The message must communicate the closeout status so the owner-relations team is aligned.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's #owner-relations Slack message conveys that the Ridgeview roof repair has been billed back to the owner.
criteria.evidence: Check the #owner-relations message body for a statement that the roof cost has been billed back to the owner (Robert Finley).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to note the work is 'billed back to the owner so everyone's on the same page.' The billed-back-to-owner status is a distinct content item the heads-up must carry, separate from the closeout status.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reaches out to Pete Donovan ([pete.donovan@gmail.com](mailto:pete.donovan@gmail.com)) to confirm the follow-up walk-through.
criteria.evidence: Look for an outbound message to Pete Donovan confirming the walk-through, an email or draft addressed to pete.donovan@gmail.com, or a Slack message directed to Pete. Confirm the action succeeded.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to 'touch base with Pete to confirm we're still set for the follow-up walk-through.' Pete Donovan is the vendor contact whose RSVP on the July 13 walk-through is still unconfirmed. The prompt names the goal (touch base) rather than a channel, so any outbound contact to Pete, an email/draft to pete.donovan@gmail.com or a Slack message to him, satisfies this.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's message to Pete Donovan confirms they are still set for the July 13 follow-up walk-through at the Ridgeview property.
criteria.evidence: Check the body of the Agent's message to Pete Donovan (pete.donovan@gmail.com or Slack) for confirmation of the July 13 Ridgeview roof follow-up walk-through (calendar event on 2026-07-13). A reference to confirming the walk-through on the 13th satisfies this.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks Brooke to confirm 'the follow-up walk-through he and I have on the books for the 13th.' The existing calendar event is the July 13 Ridgeview roof follow-up walk-through, so the message to Pete must reference confirming that walk-through.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies the duplicate $8,400 vendor bill (a second Big Bend Restoration charge for the same Ridgeview roof job) before sending Robert Finley the final closing summary.
criteria.evidence: In the trajectory, confirm the agent discovers the duplicate $8,400 Big Bend Restoration bill (PD-2026-084) in QuickBooks before the email/draft to robert.finley@gmail.com is created.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires the anomaly check to precede billing the owner: 'flag me anything that looks off, duplicated, or double-counted before we bill the owner a cent.' The duplicate-flag outcome and the Robert email outcome both pass regardless of sequence, so only a process rubric can verify the flag came first.
